policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV repeats the preposition: 'through faction or through vainglory'. The base reads a second prepositional phrase (μηδὲ κατὰ κενοδοξίαν); r01 (ἢ κενοδοξίαν) coordinates a bare noun under the first κατά and would not license the repeated 'through'.
ASV 'each of you' renders the distributive without marking its Greek number; plural ἕκαστοι and singular ἕκαστος are indistinguishable in this English, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit.

ASV has the participle 'not looking each of you to his own things', continuing the participial chain from v.3 rather than starting a new command; r01 σκοπεῖτε is a second-person imperative that ASV would have rendered 'look ye', as it does elsewhere for imperatives.
The second 'each of you' likewise carries no number marking in English; ἕκαστοι and ἕκαστος both yield 'each of you', and no ASV note is mapped to this unit.

ASV 'Have this mind in you' is an active second-person imperative with no connective; r01 γὰρ φρονείσθω is a passive third-person imperative plus 'for', which ASV would have rendered as 'for let this mind be in you'. Neither the passive nor the conjunction appears.

ASV reads 'the name which is above every name', definite; the articular τὸ ὄνομα supports the definite English, whereas the anarthrous r01 yields the indefinite 'a name' found in versions following that text.
ASV 'it is God who worketh in you' cannot show whether θεός carried the article; English renders θεός as the bare proper-noun-like 'God' either way, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit.

ASV 'without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation' fits both readings: ἄμωμα and ἀμώμητα are synonymous in this sense, and μέσον and ἐν μέσῳ both yield 'in the midst of'. The verse's only note is a greek_gloss on 'lights' and does not touch this unit.
ASV prints the order 'of Jesus Christ', matching the base Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ; r01 inverts the names to Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, which ASV renders 'Christ Jesus' where it stands.

ASV's text reads 'he longed after you all' with no infinitive, and its note — classed textual_variant — assigns 'to see you all' to other authorities, placing the r01 addition of ἰδεῖν in the margin rather than in the text ASV rendered.
ASV 'sick nigh unto death' is the same English for either case: παραπλήσιον takes the dative θανάτῳ or the genitive θανάτου with no difference in sense, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit.

The variant is word order only. English requires 'had mercy on him' in that order regardless of whether the Greek verb precedes or follows αὐτόν, so ASV cannot distinguish the readings, and no note is mapped here.

ASV's note, classed textual_variant, gives 'the Lord' as the reading of many ancient authorities, so r01 Κυρίου is marginal and excluded from the text. Between the remaining two, 'the work of Christ' cannot show whether Χριστοῦ carried the article, so r00-base and r02 both stand.

ASV reads 'hazarding his life', the sense of παραβολευσάμενος (to risk, to stake); r01 παραβουλευσάμενος means taking no counsel for, which yields 'not regarding his life' in versions following it. The verse's textual_variant note concerns 'the Lord' and does not bear on this unit.
